title: AI Demand Lifts SanDisk's First Quarter Data Center Revenue to $4.8B
summary:
SanDisk shares declined 9.3% in premarket trading on Oct. 30, despite the company posting first-quarter results that surpassed analyst projections. Revenue for the quarter grew 378% year-over-year to $11.03B, beating the $10.64B forecast, while adjusted earnings per share of $49.51 outperformed the expected $46.22. The growth was led by the company's data center segment, which generated $4.8B in revenue, a 61% increase from the previous quarter, as hyperscalers and AI infrastructure providers expanded their NAND storage requirements.

The company forecast second-quarter adjusted earnings per share between $55 and $57 and revenue of $12.2B to $12.6B. To broaden its investor base, SanDisk announced an 8-for-1 stock split effective Nov. 19, alongside $5B in share buybacks for approximately 3.2M shares. While SanDisk's CEO stated that AI-driven demand for memory is structural and likely to persist beyond 2030, the company's consumer business remains a drag, with revenue falling 39% year-over-year to $397M.

selectedTweets.text:
$SNdK just did it again!!!

Revenue came in at $11.0bn against $10.6bn expected, above the top of its own guide. EPS was $49.51 against $46.22. Operating income was $8.9bn on $11bn of sales. For a freaking memory company, that's absurd.

The number to circle is the data center $4.8bn, up 61% in a single quarter. Two years ago data center was barely part of Sandisk. Now it's over 40% of sales, and it's growing faster than anything else. AI doesn't just need memory to train models. It needs fast storage to serve them to billions of people, and that's flash.

They also guided up $12.4bn of revenue and $56 of EPS, both ahead of the Street. The worry last quarter was that supply was catching up and pricing would fade. It hasn't. Samsung, SK hynix, Microsoft and now Sandisk are all saying the same thing this week.

Add an 8 for 1 split to bring more buyers in. The memory supercycle just getting started. PT $2,700. Overweight.

selectedTweets.text:
8 things that were meaningful but not in the $SNDK release:

1. supply is spoken for: ~50% of bits under multi year (NBM) deals for FY27, ~2/3 for FY28, and that share is going higher
2. the NBM pipeline now exceeds sandisk's supply through the end of the decade
3. customers say they underestimated how much NAND they need. one of the biggest has signed a second tranche, others are in talks
4. calendar 2027: data center bit demand ~+40% YoY and over 55% of the nand market, after more than doubling in 2026
5. Q1 growth was ~60% volume, ~40% price. the Q2 guide assumes modest like for like price increases, and pricing keeps rising modestly through the year
6. no supply response: bit growth stays mid to high teens, no plan to speed up node transitions
7. NAND run in SLC mode is being tested as a DRAM substitute at a 20 to 40x cost gap. each SLC bit uses 3 to 4 bits of TLC/QLC supply. architecture talks, not sales yet
8. first HBF die taped out and in fab, samples next calendar year. still not in the long term model

@SanDisk
